title: QueryKey
subtitle: Query key type definition
description: Type definition for query keys. Query keys are unique identifiers for queries and can be strings, arrays, or objects.

rows.name: string
rows.description: Simple string identifier for the query.

rows.name: readonly (string | number)[]
rows.description: Readonly array of strings and numbers for hierarchical identification.

behavior.title: Unique Identification
behavior.description: Query keys must be unique to identify different queries

behavior.title: Serializable
behavior.description: Query keys are serialized for cache storage and comparison

behavior.title: Hierarchical
behavior.description: Array and object keys support hierarchical identification

behavior.title: Type Safe
behavior.description: Full TypeScript support with proper type inference

dos: Use descriptive and meaningful query keys
Use array keys for hierarchical identification
Use object keys for complex structured identification
Keep query keys consistent across your application
donts: Don't use query keys that change on every render
Don't use complex objects that are hard to serialize
Don't use query keys that contain sensitive data
Don't use query keys that are too long or complex

callouts.title: Key Uniqueness
callouts.content: Query keys must be unique to identify different queries. Use descriptive and meaningful keys that clearly identify the data being fetched.
